text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear opening claim and repeated stance against driverless cars","quality":"thesis clarity","description":"It states a definite position early and returns to it consistently throughout the essay."},{"evidence":"“there are drivers that enjoy driving” and “I enjoy having control of where my vehicle goes”","quality":"personal engagement","description":"It uses firsthand-sounding interest and preference to make the argument feel more immediate and purposeful."},{"evidence":"working out comparison and train analogy","quality":"developed analogy","description":"It uses comparisons to explain how driverless cars might weaken driving skills and reduce freedom."},{"evidence":"safety, liability, roadwork, sensor failure, boredom","quality":"argument breadth","description":"It considers several different objections instead of relying on only one main reason."},{"evidence":"“lawmakers know that safety is best achieved with alert drivers”","quality":"textual support integration","description":"It weaves article language into its claims more often and uses that evidence to back up the position."},{"evidence":"conclusion questions and final restatement","quality":"counterargument handling","description":"It acknowledges positives and then responds to them before ending with a clear reaffirmation of its stance."}]}
